author: IGN
description:
In celebration of Resident Evil’s 30th anniversary, we’re looking back on the survival horror games that never escaped Capcom’s walls. The stories of a culled sequel, a struggling Game Boy port, the prequel designed for a failed Nintendo 64 peripheral, and the many, many canceled versions of Resident Evil 4.

Resident Evil has often punched above its weight, but ambitious attempts to put the survival horror series on Nintendo's Game Boy and N64DD led to two famously canceled projects. Meanwhile, on the PS1, before Capcom finally created Leon and Claire's nightmare in the RPD, Resident Evil 2 was a very different game. We take a look at Hideki Kamiya's canceled Resident Evil "1.5" prototype.

#ign #residentevil
title: The Canceled Resident Evil Games You Never Got to Play

Deep within the quarries south of Howling Hill lies a cryptic challenge that has man Freeswords scratching their heads. The Dragon’s Stone Chamber is more than just a hidden room; it’s a multi-stage environmental puzzle that requires you to track down ancient murals across the Akene region to unlock the secrets within. In this guide, we’ll show you exactly where to find the hidden entrance, how to decipher the mural map, and the precise orientation for the sun, scorpion, and spiral dials needed to claim your rewards.

#IGN #Gaming

author: IGN
description:
Unlocking every skill in Crimson Desert requires a massive amount of Sealed Abyss Artifacts, but some of the challenges required to unseal them are surprisingly cryptic. If you’ve been struggling to figure out exactly how to "slide" 50 meters for the artifact near Bloomwood Ranch, we’ve got you covered. In this guide, we break down the specific location, the mount requirements, and the hidden mechanics you’ll need to master—including why your horse’s drift ability is the secret to finishing this trial.

This Crimson Desert walkthrough provides a step-by-step guide to the Sliding Down the Slope challenge found east of Bloomwood Ranch. We cover how to reach Level 3 horse training for the drift skill, the best slope near Howling Hill to attempt the run, and the specific controller inputs for Xbox, PlayStation, and PC. Learn how to manage your horse’s stamina while drifting and use map markers to measure your 50m distance precisely.

#IGN #Gaming
title: Crimson Desert: How to Slide 50m in (Sliding Down the Slope Guide)

author: IGN
description:
MLB The Show 26 reviewed by Gabriel Moss on PlayStation 5, also available on Xbox Series X|S.

MLB The Show 26 is a competent, iterative update to a series that has been making competent, iterative updates for the better part of a decade. The Trade Hub is a genuine improvement, Road to the Show's amateur phase is the most fleshed-out it's ever been, and Diamond Dynasty launches with more to do than any previous entry. But the visuals haven't evolved, the story in Road to the Show is still absent, cross-play has rough edges, and the undisclosed 20-card ownership cap feels like a step backward for the game's most dedicated no-money-spent community. If you skipped the last two or three entries, there's enough here to justify coming back. If you bought The Show 25, you already own most of this game.

#ign #gaming
title: MLB The Show 26 Review

author: IGN
description:
1348 Ex Voto reviewed by Jarrett Green on PC.

1348 Ex Voto is sick with its own pestilence. Every attempt it makes to upend the status quo for stories like this either goes criminally unexplored, is undercommitted to, or was never really deep to begin with. The rigid mission structure makes poor use of the beautiful areas throughout, giving you space to explore but nothing all that interesting to do otherwise. And every few minutes, you’ll have to plod through soupy, boring combat that never changes no matter how many options to modify small parts of it exist. The best parts of this package – a great setting, picturesque landscapes, and some truly standout acting – would be better served without all the video game bits around them.

#IGN #Gaming
title: 1348 Ex Voto Review
